## Breaking change

## Proposed change
This changes the entry setup logic. It will only bail out if the connection to the server failed.
Handling the initial state will be processed in the background AFTER the entry setup is done.
This will fix situations where the connection/server is slow to send the initial state or a really large mesh (where processing the initial state takes a long time).

## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
After enabling the websocket server and ensuring that zwave-js has completed interviewing devices, adding the zwave-js integration fails to connect on the first try, and subsequent tries do not discover devices

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 2021.2.0.dev20210123
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): has never worked
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): OS 5.10 dev
- Integration causing this issue: Z-Wave JS
- Link to integration documentation on our website: 

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

## Additional information
comments:
I think I've figured out why the initial failure occurs.
The Z-Wave-JS link takes longer than 10 seconds to be fully initialized, but there is a 10 second timeout on the connection.
So, I think there are 2 issues here. First, the 10 second timer needs to be longer, and second, if it times out it should fail, not leave the integration's configuration half-built.

review_comments: Since the library creates a task that is not tracked by home assistant for the callback, we'll now not wait to fire the home assistant start event until all platforms are loaded and existing nodes discovered. Maybe that's ok?
I suppose we have no other solution to tackle this other than wait for a REALLY long time...
